lines.say: Borrow a hundred acorns, owe a hundred and five. Why?

lines.text: Because interest is rent. You're paying to use someone else's acorns.
lines.say: Because interest is rent. You're paying to use someone else's acorns.

lines.text: Rent pays for waiting, and for inflation, since acorns may buy less later.
lines.say: Rent pays for waiting, and for inflation, since acorns may buy less later.

lines.text: And risk: the chipmunk borrower might never pay back.
lines.say: And risk: the chipmunk borrower might never pay back.

lines.text: Our math: 100 acorns at 5% for a year makes 105.
lines.say: Our math: a hundred acorns at five percent for a year makes a hundred and five.

lines.text: Banks rent both ways. In 2026, savings paid 0.38%; cards charged 22.36%.
lines.say: Banks rent both ways. In twenty twenty-six, savings paid zero point three eight percent; cards charged twenty-two point three six percent.

lines.text: Mortgage rent moves too: 2.96% in 2021, 6.6% in 2025.
lines.say: Mortgage rent moves too: two point nine six percent in twenty twenty-one, six point six percent in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The Fed's base rent was 3.75% to 4% as of October 2026.
lines.say: The Fed's base rent was three point seven five to four percent as of October twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: So lend, and you collect rent. Borrow, and you pay it.
lines.say: So lend, and you collect rent. Borrow, and you pay it.

post.title: Why squirrel lends 100 acorns and wants 105 back
post.ig:
Squirrel lends 100 acorns and wants 105 back. Why?
Interest is rent: the price of using someone else's money for a while. It pays for waiting, inflation and risk.
In Oct 2026 the average savings rate was 0.38% (FDIC). In Aug 2026 card balances were charged 22.36% (Fed G.19).
The 30-year mortgage averaged 2.96% in 2021 and 6.6% in 2025 (Freddie Mac). The Fed's target range was 3.75%-4% as of Oct 2026.
Sources: Federal Reserve, FDIC, Freddie Mac via FRED.
